subject: [ACME] Urgent: sudden spike in 5xx/429s — token validation noise and retry surge

Subject: Spike: 5xx/429s & timeouts impacting batch ingest

Hi Grace,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx and 429 responses hitting our ingestion pipeline around 08:45 PST this morning. Throughput dropped by ~40% and multiple downstream jobs retried aggressively which created a retry storm.

Symptoms we've observed:
- ~30% of requests to /v1/generate returning 5xx or 429s for valid API keys.
- Some requests that were successful then started failing with 401/5xx intermittently.
- Timestamps in our logs show repeated token validation failures referencing JWT "exp" but tokens are within TTL.

We've attached a short trace (acme_trace_2027-02-15.log). Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (clock sync, token validation rules, gateway config)? This is P1 for us — our ingest queues are backing up.

Thanks,
Alice

Platform Reliability, ACME Corp

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429s & timeouts impacting batch ingest — quick triage

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed elevated 5xx/429 counts across the auth-gateway cluster starting 08:43 PST. Rate matched ACME's traces.
- Correlated logs show many failures originate from our JWT validation layer where we log "token expired" and "signature verification failed" but token payloads indicate valid exp/iat values.
- We also see repeated upstream 504s from the internal token-introspect service when it experienced brief GC pauses.
- Crucially: the gateway code path currently maps some token-introspection errors and unexpected validation exceptions to 5xx/429 responses instead of a canonical 401 with clear error. That misclassification has caused ACME's clients to retry aggressively.

Attachments: jwt_drift_analysis.pdf (short analysis), sample snippets inlined below.

Sample log excerpt:
[2027-02-15T08:44:12.321Z] gw-13 auth: jwt_validation error=signature_mismatch token_id=xxx payload_exp=170795... result=INTROSPECT_ERROR
[2027-02-15T08:44:12.322Z] gw-13 response: status=502 mapped_from=INTROSPECT_ERROR

Immediate mitigation applied at 09:58 PST:
- Changed gateway mapping: introspect/validation exceptions -> 401 with X-Auth-Err header for known introspection transient failures.
- Deployed a short-lived circuit-breaker to limit retries and added response hints to discourage aggressive client retries.

Impact since mitigations: error rate dropped ~65% at the gateway, ACME reports fewer downstream retries. Full root cause still under investigation (hypothesis: clock skew + transient token-introspect instability + mapping bug).

Next steps:
- Run clock drift audit across token-issuing fleet and ACME's suggested token TTL/clock sync window (Marissa).
- Patch mapping logic to avoid converting introspect failures into 5xx (Marissa/Infra).
- Run a canary change to reduce GC pressure on token-introspect service (Infra).
- Draft customer-facing summary and credit guidance (Grace/Jonas).

I'll continue with logs and a short doc.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429s & timeouts impacting batch ingest — exec summary for ACME and internal

Folks — preparing a short executive summary for ACME and our CRO. Draft below; please flag edits. We want to be transparent, own the outage, and give a clear remediation & timeline.

Executive summary (draft):
- What happened: starting ~08:43 PST, ACME saw a surge of 5xx/429 responses and downstream retry storms.
- Why it happened (interim finding): a cascade of transient failures in our token-introspect service combined with a gateway mapping bug caused valid-looking token validation errors to be surfaced as 5xx/429 rather than 401. Additionally, small clock skew between token issuers and introspection clients made some tokens appear invalid during the window.
- Immediate impact: ~40% throughput reduction for ACME ingest traffic and elevated retry traffic causing downstream job backpressure.
- Immediate mitigations performed: mapping fix to return 401 for introspection errors, short circuit-breaker deployed, GC tuning canary for introspect service. Error rate down ~65%.
- Proposed next steps and ETA:
  1) Full root-cause postmortem within 72 hours (Marissa).
  2) Permanent mapping fix + unit tests in the next 48 hours (Marissa/Infra).
  3) Clock drift audit and guidance to customers on acceptable clock window + optional token refresh strategy in 48 hours (Infra/Customer Engineering).
  4) Outreach + proposed credit plan by EOD (Grace/Jonas).

Can we agree to send this to ACME at 12:30 PST? Marissa — can you attach the short analysis (jwt_drift_analysis.pdf) and confirm the GC canary schedule?

— Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Reliability & Escalations
Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — quick update and plan. Thank you for the trace.

What we've done so far:
- Identified that some token-introspection/transient validation errors were being returned as 5xx/429 instead of 401; this caused client retries and a retry amplification loop.
- Applied an emergency mapping change and short circuit-breaker which reduced the error rate by ~65% and stabilized your throughput.

What we're doing next (concrete):
1) We will run a full clock-drift audit across our token-issuer and introspection fleet and share results by EOD tomorrow.
2) Permanent code and test fix to mapping logic (ETA 48h).
3) GC tuning canary on token-introspect service (rolling this evening).
4) Customer communication & proposed SLA credit options — we'll send a formal note by EOD today.

Attachments: incident_comm_plan.docx (internal plan); jwt_drift_analysis.pdf (short technical note).

Please let me know if you want a bridge now; otherwise we'll schedule a 30-min recap tomorrow at 10:00 PST.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the impact and are treating this with top priority.

Best,
